newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-Gaullist chief told to reimburse official funds.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Gaullist chief told to reimburse official funds.

text.p: A French prosecutor on Thursday ordered former Gaullist party secretary-general Jean-Francois Mancel to reimburse 600,000 francs ($100,000) for food and household products he billed to a local authority he headed but which were for his private use.

Justice sources said prosecutor Odile Valette told Mancel, president of the elected general council of the Oise departement north of Paris, she would not level criminal charges since he had ceased such purchases and agreed to reimburse those already made.

Valette said she would not ask Mancel to reimburse several hundred thousand francs worth of champagne bottles purchased in the same circumstances over several years because these were legitimate expenses for official receptions.
A legal probe into Mancel's spending had been opened as a result of an official audit last year.

Mancel's functions as head of the Oise council were separate from his role as secretary-general of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) party, a post he resigned after a crushing centre-right general election defeat in June.
